stories.title: S&P projects 7% GDP growth for India, warns El Nino could raise food prices
stories.summary: S&P Global Ratings forecasts India’s GDP to grow about 7 percent in the current fiscal year and again in the next fiscal year. The agency notes that an El Nino event is likely to push food prices higher, adding inflationary pressure and increasing input costs that could be passed on to consumers.

stories.title: Rupee slips to 92.91 per dollar amid corporate dollar demand and profit‑taking
stories.summary: The Indian rupee settled at 92.91 against the U.S. dollar on Monday, ending a five‑day rise after major corporations increased demand for dollars and traders took profits. It had earlier peaked at 92.44. Weak performance in domestic equities added to the bearish tone, while analysts still see a positive bias for stocks and the rupee.

stories.title: India-EU trade deal likely to be signed on December 16
stories.summary: Described as the 'mother of all deals', the FTA will provide duty-free access to the EU for 93% of India's exports, while making imports of luxury cars and wines from the bloc cheaper. Together, India and the EU account for 25% of global GDP and about one-third of international trade, valued at $11 trillion of the $33 trillion global trade market.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
stories.previousTitle: India and EU expected to sign free‑trade pact on Dec 16
stories.previousSummary: An Indian official said the free‑trade agreement with the 27‑member European Union is likely to be signed on 16 December, after the two sides concluded negotiations on 27 January. The deal would grant duty‑free access for about 93 % of Indian exports to the EU and make imports of luxury cars and wines from the bloc cheaper. Together, India and the EU account for roughly 25 % of global GDP and about one‑third of world trade.
